This racquet sits in the spin category and is designed around its primary performance strengths. The 100 in² head size boosts forgiveness and sweet spot size. The 2010 Babolat Aero Pro Lite GT excels at generating topspin thanks to its 261g weight and 100 square inch head. The lightweight frame swings easily, helping you add spin to your shots without much effort. It scores 100/100 for spin and 80/100 for power, but only 40/100 for control—expect shots to fly if you're not careful with your technique. The stiff 68 RA frame feels crisp and responsive, but players with arm issues should consider softer strings or a more flexible racquet. At net, the light weight helps with quick reactions, though the frame lacks the stability of heavier racquets on hard-hit balls. This racquet works best for intermediate players who already have consistent strokes and want to add more spin. Beginners may struggle with the lack of control, while advanced players might find it too light for their power game. Used by Rafael Nadal, though his version is customized with added weight.

Updates to shaft geometry and NF2 Tech improve feel and comfort, making this an ideal option for players seeking speed, spin, and accessible power.

The Wilson Burn 100LS V5 is the lighter 280 g Spin Effect version of the Burn 100 family. It keeps the 100 in² head and open 18x16 pattern, giving intermediate players easier racquet-head speed, free depth and heavy topspin without jumping to a full 300 g Burn frame. It is more stable than the 100ULS but still noticeably maneuverable. The main Racqix warning is comfort: the frame is stiff at roughly 72 RA, so players with arm sensitivity should avoid tight full-bed polyester and use soft poly, hybrid, synthetic gut or multifilament setups.

The Wilson Burn 100ULS V5 is the lightest adult Burn V5 frame and is built for easy racquet-head speed, free power and spin. The 100 in² head and 260 g unstrung weight make it accessible for beginners, intermediates, rising juniors and players who want a lighter adult frame. The 18x16 Spin Effect pattern gives the ball more launch and rotation, but it can also reduce directional control and string durability. Because the frame is fairly stiff, Racqix should steer comfort-sensitive players toward multifilament, synthetic gut or a soft hybrid before recommending a full stiff polyester setup.
